pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: The triad of unexplained neurovisceral symptoms (colicky abdominal pain + neuropsychiatric crisis + autonomic instability), profound hyponatremia, urine darkening on ambient light exposure (oxidation of porphobilinogen to porphobilin), and catastrophic motor deterioration following administration of CYP-inducing porphyrinogenic medications (TMP-SMX and haloperidol). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis caused by a deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD / HMBS). Fasting (caloric restriction) or porphyrinogenic drugs strongly induce hepatic ALAS1 via peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α). Because of the downstream enzymatic block, neurotoxic intermediates—delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—rapidly accumulate, causing widespread central, autonomic, and peripheral motor axonal neuropathy.
